items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Risk severity: high for fleet-wide go-live, new public exposure, and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Evidence timestamp: 2026-10-01T04:50:05.408Z. The baseline covers 61 managed sites, but fleet-doctor has no run, checks, findings, or site results; operations has no deploy, uptime, or error-sweep results; and authentication/access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS configuration, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness are unevidenced. TLS expiration evidence shows no certificates expiring within 30 days, but does not establish complete TLS posture. Compliance is technical-only: 35 pass, 20 fail, 6 unknown; it is not certification. Exact decision: preserve public-exposure and security-sensitive release gates, do not claim clearance or a clean bill of health, and continue only bounded read-only evidence work plus constrained reversible growth. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, alter permissions or configuration, deploy, add dependencies, request duplicate telemetry, or conduct external outreach.

Security recommendation: keep SearchWoot private and block public beta, go-live, notification expansion, monetization changes, and rights outreach. Source-rights, data-flow, consent and analytics, vendor/logging, incident, accuracy, measurement, and security gates remain incomplete. No security-sensitive implementation is approved until dated evidence supports access boundaries, secrets handling, isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness.
